{"summary": "I added `word_count(text)` to `textutils.py`, and all 3 tests pass when I run `python -m unittest`.

It lower-cases the text and treats any run of letters, digits and apostrophes as a word. Everything else counts as a separator, including underscores. It returns a plain `dict` of word counts. Unicode letters count as letters, so `café` is one word, and a run made only of apostrophes is skipped. `words()` is unchanged.

Apostrophes at the start or end of a word are kept as part of it, so a quoted `'hello'` counts as the word `'hello'`, not `hello`.

I added two tests to `test_textutils.py`. One checks mixed case, punctuation, digits and contractions (`it's`, `o'clock`). The other checks empty input and input that is only punctuation.", "suggestions": ["Strip apostrophes at the start and end of words so quoted words count as the bare word"]}
